title: Multinomial PMF in Mathlib: Strategy and Dependencies
content: The file answers the open question "can the multinomial distribution be integrated into Mathlib's PMF framework?" affirmatively, by an explicit, fully verified construction. Mathlib supplies `Nat.multinomial`, the `piAntidiag`-based multinomial theorem `Finset.sum_pow_eq_sum_piAntidiag`, the `PMF` type, and `ENNReal` arithmetic; the file builds the `Composition` support type, the ENNReal normalization, the `PMF` instance, and the distributional properties (support, marginal, mean, covariance) on top.
mathContext: The construction packages $P(X=k)=\binom{n}{k_1,\dots,k_r}\prod_i p_i^{k_i}$ as a `PMF` over the simplex $\{k:\sum_i k_i=n\}$, with normalization $\sum_k P(X=k)=(\sum_i p_i)^n=1$.

title: Composition: The Support Type of the Multinomial, with Fintype Instance
content: `Composition α s n` bundles a count function `counts : α → ℕ`, the constraint `∑_{i∈s} counts i = n`, and the zero-outside condition. Its `Fintype` instance (lines 61-72) is proved — not a sorry — by transport along an explicit `Equiv` with the subtype `↥(s.piAntidiag n)`, using `Finset.mem_piAntidiag` to translate between the structure's two fields and piAntidiag membership.
mathContext: The support of $\mathrm{Multinomial}(n,p)$ on alphabet $s$ is $\{k:s\to\mathbb N\mid\sum_{i\in s}k_i=n\}$, which is exactly `Finset.piAntidiag s n`. Wrapping it as a `Fintype` is the prerequisite for `PMF.mk`.

title: The Multinomial Mass Function in ℝ≥0∞
content: `multinomialPMFVal s p n k = (Nat.multinomial s k.counts : ℝ≥0∞) * ∏ i ∈ s, p i ^ k.counts i` is the mass function valued in the extended nonnegative reals, the type Mathlib's `PMF` requires.

title: Multinomial Theorem = PMF Normalization
content: `multinomialPMF_sum_eq_one` proves $\sum_k \mathrm{multinomialPMFVal}(k)=1$ when $\sum_i p_i=1$. The Composition-indexed sum is transported to a `piAntidiag` sum (via the sibling file's bridge), folded into a power by `Finset.sum_pow_eq_sum_piAntidiag`, and closed with `∑p=1`, `1^n=1`. This is the heart of the PMF construction.
mathContext: The same identity $(\sum_i p_i)^n=\sum_k\binom{n}{k}\prod_i p_i^{k_i}$ is simultaneously the multinomial theorem and the normalization $\sum_k P(X=k)=1$ — the bridge between combinatorics and probability.

title: The PMF Instance via PMF.mk
content: `multinomialPMF` packages `multinomialPMFVal` with the normalization proof into a genuine `PMF (Composition α s n)`, converting the `Finset.sum = 1` statement into the required `HasSum … 1` via `hasSum_fintype`.
mathContext: `PMF α` is `{f : α → ℝ≥0∞ // HasSum f 1}`; for a `Fintype` index, `HasSum f c ↔ ∑ a, f a = c`.

title: PMF Value and Support (both fully proved)
content: `multinomialPMF_apply` is `rfl` (the PMF's value field is the mass function). `multinomialPMF_support` characterizes the support: the value is nonzero iff every counted outcome has nonzero probability. Proved using that the multinomial coefficient is a positive natural and that ℝ≥0∞ has no zero divisors, so a product is nonzero iff every factor is, with `p i ^ k = 0 ↔ p i = 0 ∧ k ≠ 0`.

title: The Marginal of Xᵢ is Binomial(n, pᵢ)
content: `multinomial_marginal_binomial` proves that summing the multinomial weight over all compositions with `k i = m` gives the binomial PMF `C(n,m)·pᵢᵐ·(1−pᵢ)ⁿ⁻ᵐ`. The proof is a reindexing bijection (`Finset.sum_nbij'`) that zeroes the i-th coordinate, identifying compositions of n with kᵢ=m on s with compositions of n−m on s∖{i}; `Nat.multinomial_insert` splits off the factor `C(n,m)`, and `Finset.sum_pow_eq_sum_piAntidiag` on s∖{i} contributes `(∑_{j≠i} pⱼ)ⁿ⁻ᵐ = (1−pᵢ)ⁿ⁻ᵐ`.
mathContext: Marginalising the multinomial over one coordinate collapses the other categories into a single 'failure' outcome of probability $1-p_i$, recovering $X_i\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(n,p_i)$.

title: The Absorption Identity — the Combinatorial Engine
content: `multinomial_absorb` proves the key recurrence `kᵢ·multinomial(s,k) = n·multinomial(s, update k i (kᵢ−1))` for a composition k of n with kᵢ≥1. The proof avoids ℕ-division: it cancels the common positive factor `(kᵢ−1)!·∏_{j≠i}(kⱼ!)` after applying `Nat.multinomial_spec` to both sides and `Nat.mul_factorial_pred`. Both the mean and the cross moment are reductions to the multinomial theorem driven by this single identity.
mathContext: From $\binom{n}{k}=n!/\prod_j k_j!$ one gets $k_i\binom{n}{k}=n\binom{n-1}{k-e_i}$ — lowering $k_i$ by one absorbs the factor $k_i$ into $n$.

title: Mean E[Xᵢ] = n·pᵢ via the Absorption Bijection
content: `multinomial_mean` proves `∑_k kᵢ·multinomial(s,k)·∏pⱼ^kⱼ = n·pᵢ`. After discarding the kᵢ=0 terms, `Finset.sum_nbij'` lowers kᵢ by one (the weighted absorption identity `multinomial_absorb_weighted` turns the summand into `n·pᵢ` times the (n−1)-trial weight), and the remaining sum is the total mass `(∑p)ⁿ⁻¹ = 1`.
mathContext: $E[X_i]=\sum_k k_i P(X=k)=n p_i\sum_{k'}P_{n-1}(X=k')=n p_i$ — the absorption identity makes this a one-line reduction to normalization at $n-1$.

title: Cross Moment and Covariance Cov(Xᵢ,Xⱼ) = −n·pᵢ·pⱼ
content: `multinomial_cross_moment` proves `E[XᵢXⱼ] = n(n−1)pᵢpⱼ` for i≠j by lowering Xᵢ via one absorption bijection — the surviving kⱼ factor rides along unchanged (since j≠i) and the reduced sum is exactly `n·pᵢ` times the mean of Xⱼ over n−1 trials, i.e. `n·pᵢ·(n−1)·pⱼ`. `multinomial_covariance` then expands `Cov = E[XᵢXⱼ] − E[Xᵢ]E[Xⱼ] = n(n−1)pᵢpⱼ − n²pᵢpⱼ = −n·pᵢ·pⱼ`, the total mass `∑w=1` supplying the subtracted term.
mathContext: The negative correlation is forced by the simplex constraint $\sum_i X_i=n$: more of one outcome means less of another. The cross moment reuses the mean, so the whole moment structure rests on the single absorption identity.

title: Concrete Example: Six Distinct Dice Faces
content: `dice_six_rolls_all_different` computes `multinomial({0,…,5}, fun _ => 1) = 6! = 720` by kernel `decide` (not `native_decide`), so the example — and the whole file — incurs no `Lean.ofReduceBool` axiom. The probability of seeing each face once in six fair rolls is 720/6⁶ = 720/46656.
